culture_description: The Reefstriders read broken water as others read roads. Fishing crews, pearl-divers and shoal pilots divide the coast into customary working grounds, marked by shell cairns and remembered soundings. House Reefhook holds the crown through its obligation to guide returning boats and recover crews from the reefs. A wreck's cargo is divided only after the rescuers and bereaved households receive their shares. Pearls buy foreign iron and favor, but a pilot who sells a guest's safe passage loses the protection of every harbor. Before a deep dive, the first unbroken shell is returned to the water for the Hunger Below.
ruler_story: Skrezz Reefhook, the Wreck-Taker, won his name at the Lantern Shoals. With the harbor boats scattered by a squall, he led a relief crew through a submerged channel and brought home the stranded fishers, then stripped their abandoned hulls before the next tide. He made the salvaged timber into boats for households that had lost their catch. Quick with a joke and quicker to spot a bargaining weakness, Skrezz cultivates visiting captains personally. He spends tomorrow's pearl revenue freely and leaves his court to settle the accounts.
dynasty_story: House Reefhook traces its authority to Zrekk's first chain of rescue beacons, maintained by each harbor household in return for pilotage rights. Its saying is 'Bring the crew home; reckon the cargo after.' Skrezz wears the house's split-shell clasp rather than a jeweled crown. His older brother Krizzek is the adult dynastic successor under the existing strength law; in court he presses the claims of fishing households against Skrezz's costly foreign friendships. Consort Zikka of House Shoalcut brings ties to the pilot families. Their young children Zikrat and Skrizza make the future of the rescue line a matter of public concern.
nation_story: Reefhook's growing settlements need safe fishing grounds, dependable buyers and grain from larger islands. Pearl wealth arrives in bursts, while nets and boats need repair every season. Skrezz wants the other crowns to treat Reefhook's pilots as indispensable partners. Harbor elders fear that selling their soundings will surrender the very advantage that keeps the island independent. Divers demand a fair share of rich finds; widowed households expect the house to honor its rescue obligations even in a lean year. Reefhook can turn navigation and trade into influence, but every lost boat tests the crown's claim to rule.
event_description: Skrezz Reefhook, the Wreck-Taker, lays a split shell beside the foreign captains' gifts. His house promises that crews come home before cargo is counted. Krizzek asks how that promise survives if our best pilots serve another crown; Zikka's Shoalcut kin ask who will pay for the beacons. Pearls and safe passage give our small kingdom a voice among larger neighbors. An alliance may protect our fisheries, and voluntary vassalage may offer security at the usual price in obligations. Skrezz would bargain from the shoals, but the fishing households must live with his terms.
event_answer: Our soundings are worth a seat at their table.
